title: Perfect sufficient rule — ministry and Spirit stay; no second rule
source_text: XIII. Quandoquidem autem omnia quae ad fidem pertinent Scriptura sacra continentur, quomodo jam expositum est, inde colligitur Scripturam esse fidei regulam perfectam & sufficientem. Quae tamen sufficientia non excludit necessitatem ministerii Ecclesiastici, quo, juxta ordinem a Deo constitutum, doctrina caelestis ex Scriptura hauritur, & fideli populo per suos pastores & doctores traditur: tum quoque interni Spiritus magisterii, quo fideles ducuntur in notitiam doctrinae ex Scriptura haustae atque propositae, & sine quo illam discernere, & salutariter amplecti non possunt. Sed ista Scripturae sacrae perfectio & sufficientia, excludit solummodo necessitatem alterius regulae, quam Scripturae sacrae adjungi necesse sit, ut integram fidei doctrinam habeamus. Unde patet nihil agere Ecclesiae Romanae Doctores, qui nobis ad salutem Scripturam non sufficere inde probare conantur, quod alioqui frustra foret ministerium Ecclesiasticum, cujus tamen necessitas in ipsa sacra Scriptura commendatur.
pass_a_gloss: But since all things which pertain to faith are contained by sacred Scripture, in the manner now set forth, from that it is gathered that Scripture is a perfect and sufficient rule of faith. Which sufficiency, however, does not exclude the necessity of the Ecclesiastical ministry, by which, according to the order constituted by God, heavenly doctrine is drawn from Scripture, and is handed over to the faithful people through their pastors and doctors: and also of the internal magisterium of the Spirit, by which the faithful are led into knowledge of the doctrine drawn from Scripture and proposed, and without which they cannot discern it and salutarily embrace it. But that perfection and sufficiency of sacred Scripture excludes only the necessity of another rule, which it would be necessary to join to sacred Scripture in order that we may have the whole doctrine of faith. Whence it is plain that the Doctors of the Roman Church accomplish nothing, who try to prove from this that Scripture does not suffice for us unto salvation, because otherwise the Ecclesiastical ministry would be in vain, whose necessity nevertheless is commended in sacred Scripture itself.
pass_b_english: Since everything that belongs to faith is in sacred Scripture in the way already shown, Scripture is a perfect and sufficient rule of faith.

That sufficiency does not cancel the Church's ministry. By God's order, heavenly teaching is drawn from Scripture and given to the faithful through their pastors and teachers. It also does not cancel the Spirit's inward teaching, by which believers come to know the doctrine drawn from Scripture and set before them — without which they cannot discern it or embrace it for salvation.
Scripture's perfection and sufficiency shut out only one thing: the need of another rule that must be joined to Scripture before we have the whole doctrine of faith.
So Rome's doctors gain nothing when they argue that Scripture is not enough for salvation because otherwise the Church's ministry would be useless. Scripture itself urges that ministry.

choices.why: Internal Spirit teaching paired with external pastors.
